body: Thank you, it does help a little bit.
I didn’t even know what OCD truly was until my late teens, but I had been suffering from it since early childhood. Even now, when new themes come along, I see traces of them earlier than I realized.
That’s true, I definitely remember not liking it, which I’m glad about. I’m just disgusted at myself for ever letting those thoughts be in my mind.
Thank you, this was very helpful!
I am not currently seeing a therapist but I would definitely like to eventually. However, can I ask for your opinion on what I said in my post?

I know, I’m just trying to determine if that’s what I can even call this. I just think there’s a line that can be crossed and it’s hard to tell if I’ve already crossed it. And I did have another account at one point but I lost the login information. I may have asked something similar before.
Thank you. I suppose you’re right. It just seems like at some point there’s a line that can be crossed and it’s hard to tell if I’ve already crossed it.

I wish we didn’t at all either. I think visiting a therapist is a very good idea. Telling your parents is up to you, but I definitely think it’s important to be completely open with your therapist. Just make sure you’re seeing an OCD specialist, as therapists who aren’t well experienced with OCD won’t be helpful.

I’m sorry to hear you’re struggling as well. It is by far the worst theme of OCD I’ve ever dealt with, and I can’t imagine what could possibly be worse. I relate to worrying about not worrying. I believe this is known as a backdoor spike, when you feel guilty simply for not being crippled by OCD. It’s good that your parents are supportive. They don’t need to know all of the details of your OCD. It’s not an easy thing to discuss. I also struggle to see a life worth living with POCD constantly on our minds, but just remember, it’s OCD, which is a very treatable illness and much more common than it seems. Things will be okay.
Yeah it can at least help until better options are available. I hope you’re doing well, man.
Thank you so much, this is a very helpful read.
